title: A Networks and Machine Learning Approach to Determine the Best College Coaches of the 20th-21st Centuries

inputs: college game results and final margins
decisions: how team skill is separated into player and coach effects
which optimizer generates annual coach vectors
how annual ranks become career values
how far local data sensitivity can be claimed

section_map.summary: The summary compresses the sport scope, yearly network route, eigenvector ranking, coach-player separation, optimization, and century ranking.
The public explainer, technical title, and contents convert the broad coach question into data, network, separation, optimization, ranking, and testing sections.
The paper restates the all-time coach task and presents a six-step route from annual game graphs to historical coach ranking.
The assumptions fix annual team skill, multiplicative team composition, and the player-gap condition under which coaching affects a result.
The data section describes game-result collection, coach matching, standardized names, and sport-specific coverage limits.
A weighted directed graph encodes annual wins, repeated meetings, and score margins before any team ranking is calculated.
The paper contrasts degree, betweenness, closeness, and eigenvector centrality, then validates the chosen ranking against published polls.
Team skill is factorized into coach and player skill, then player gaps damp coach effect and determine the margin-likelihood expression.
The joint likelihood is converted to a squared objective, rejected methods are documented, and Powell search is retained for yearly coach vectors.
Annual top-five appearances are normalized by active years to produce the final cross-century coach lists.
Two single-game perturbations, strengths, and computational limitations bound the claimed robustness of the ranking.
The conclusion restates the graph-to-ranking route and the references expose the web and method dependencies needed to reproduce it.

assumptions.summary: Coach skill is expressed through wins and margin, so a coach whose team wins no games is not considered good by this model.
Team skill is constant within a year, despite injuries and changing player skill.
Wins over better teams improve team skill more, enabling eigenvector centrality as the annual skill measure.
Team skill is multiplicative in coach and player skill, giving each coach the same effect on each player.
Coach effect is large only when player skills are close, and is the only win-margin factor when they are similarly matched.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Game-result and coach data are collected from multiple websites, standardized, and matched through a manually created name table when source spellings differ.
Football results cover 1869-2013; basketball covers 1939-2013; baseball has tournament-game coverage from 1947-2013 in the summary and 1949-present in the technical section.
Each annual graph stores winner-to-loser edge counts and a list of score margins for repeated meetings.
Powell search is implemented in Python across each available yearly network, but no frozen game records, matching table, source snapshot, or run configuration is supplied.

models.summary: Collect game scores and coach assignments, normalize team names, and retain sport-specific coverage limits.
Represent every game in one sport-year as a winner-to-loser edge with a count and margin list.
Compare centrality measures and retain eigenvector centrality as the team-skill score.
Express team skill as coach skill times player skill before optimizing the unknown coach vector.
Diminish coach-effect magnitude when player skills differ and retain it when teams are evenly matched.
Map player and coach effects to the probability of a signed game margin.
Aggregate likelihood across annual games and minimize the equivalent displayed squared cost.
Initialize coach and player vectors and evolve them, then reject the attempt for slow convergence and nonoptimal values.
Iterate a coach-skill vector with a simplex, then reject the method after local extrema give little likelihood improvement.
Use bidirectional search along search vectors to lower the cost function for each available year.
Turn each annual optimized top-five list into an active-years-normalized career value.
Delete or reverse one recorded game and compare the resulting score and first-place rank with the unmodified run.

dependency_graph.handoff: Matched sport-year game and coach records become weighted winner-to-loser edges with margin lists.
The annual adjacency structure supplies the centrality calculation and team ranking.
Annual team centrality is treated as team skill in the coach-player factorization.
Player skill derived from team and coach skill supplies the player-gap damping term.
The damped coach effect and player effect enter the margin likelihood.
Per-game likelihoods are multiplied and rewritten as the annual squared objective.
The same objective is first attempted with the genetic algorithm.
The unresolved annual objective is next attempted with Nelder-Mead.
The failed local search motivates Powell's retained direction-set route.
Each annual Powell result contributes a top-five appearance count and active-year denominator.
The career ranking is perturbed by one deleted and one reversed game to inspect local input sensitivity.

verification.summary: The 2009-2010 basketball top ten from eigenvector centrality is compared with AP and USA Today lists, with six reported overlaps.
verification.strength: The source exposes a named comparator and a top-ten overlap.
verification.limitation: A partial poll overlap is not an independent validation of historical coach effects or the probability model.

verification.summary: Deleting a 1975 Alabama win is reported to lower the coach score by about 1% without changing first place.
verification.strength: The direction and rank response of a stated deletion are inspectable.
verification.limitation: One selected game and one outcome do not characterize data, parameter, structural, or solver robustness.

verification.summary: Reversing that game is reported to lower the Alabama coach score by about 4% and change first place.
verification.strength: The source reports a larger directed input change and its rank consequence.
verification.limitation: The perturbation has no distribution, repetitions, seed, or full-ranking response.

results_trace.summary: Powell's method is reported faster than Nelder-Mead and to lower the displayed cost over several thousand iterations.
Career value is annual top-five appearances divided by active years, yielding listed basketball, football, and baseball top fives.
The two changed-game tests produce approximately 1% and 4% reductions, with only the latter changing the first-ranked coach.
The conclusion restates the graph, eigenvector, coach-player separation, probability, annual optimization, and career-ranking chain.

contributions.summary: The six-step planned approach exposes an end-to-end route before detailed mathematics.
Winner-to-loser graph edges preserve opponent structure and score-margin payloads.
The centrality equations and poll table make team-ranking selection inspectable.
The player-gap term makes the intended coach-effect condition explicit.
The likelihood and squared objective expose the annual optimization interface.
Rejected and retained solver paths reveal a practical selection rationale.
Two directed input changes provide a bounded, visible rank-sensitivity example.

visualization_observations.summary: A two-team directed-edge illustration explains the winner-to-loser encoding before the technical paper begins.
The public explainer displays the final top-five names for the three sports.
The contents exposes the source sequence from data and network ranking to separation, optimization, ranking, testing, and conclusion.
The network diagram shows nodes as teams and edges as games, with conference clustering visible.
The centrality definition, matrix eigenvector relation, and walk series make the selected team-ranking mechanism inspectable.
The three-column top-ten table compares eigenvector centrality with AP and USA Today rankings.
Node size and darkness encode relative eigenvector centrality in the complete seasonal network.
The centered product equation connects team skill to coach and player skill.
Two margin-probability sketches and the player-gap damping expression motivate when coach effect is used.
The annual product and squared objective make the optimization handoff visible.
Three widely separated yearly top-three lists serve as the source's selected-solver output.
The career-frequency ratio and three-sport table translate annual output into the final decision artifact.
The two perturbation cases connect one changed game to score and rank response.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The explicit stepwise route makes the requested decision traceable, but award status does not prove that this organization caused the award.
The named poll comparison makes an external comparator visible, without proving independent validity of coach effects.
The source reports a directed sensitivity test rather than only asserting stability, without proving complete robustness.

weaknesses.summary: The walk-series term visibly changes from negative inverse powers to lambda^(n-1) A^n; reconcile the exponent before implementing the stated intuition.
The multiplicative team-skill relation does not state an identifiability or normalization constraint for separately recovering coach and player skill.
The source writes multiword quantities such as player effect and coach effect as italicized mathematical variables; preserve and normalize their definitions before computation.
The likelihood-to-objective equivalence is asserted after algebra without a complete parameter, normalization, and domain specification.
The source acknowledges local minima and initialization sensitivity for Powell search but supplies no repeated-start protocol, tolerance, or convergence log.
The sensitivity evidence changes one selected game in two ways; it lacks a perturbation distribution, repetitions, full-rank analysis, and source-data audit.
References identify web and method sources but do not preserve versioned game records, coach matching, processed tables, solver code, or executable run settings.

independent_extensions.summary: Publish a versioned game-and-coach data dictionary, name-matching table, coverage report, and reproducible annual graph constructor.
Specify centrality orientation, positivity condition, convergence tolerance, disconnected-graph handling, and a corrected walk-series derivation before reuse.
Add an identifiability constraint or hierarchical model for coach and player skill, then compare alternatives against held-out game outcomes.
Run seeded multi-start optimization with stopping rules, diagnostics, objective distribution, and independent out-of-sample validation.
Use repeated, stratified game perturbations and report rank intervals, top-k stability, and solver uncertainty rather than two selected changes.
